gaps.sentence: Too much time ___ (waste) on pointless meetings these days.
gaps.explanation: 'These days' signals a present general situation: is + wasted (singular 'time').

gaps.sentence: She couldn't pay because her wallet ___ (steal) at the market.
gaps.hint: earlier past action causing a past problem
gaps.explanation: The theft happened before the failed payment: past perfect passive, had been + stolen.

gaps.sentence: The parcels ___ (deliver) every morning before the shop opens.
gaps.explanation: Present simple passive (am/is/are + past participle) for regular, repeated actions: are delivered.

gaps.sentence: A cheaper version of the vaccine ___ right now.
gaps.explanation: 'Right now' requires present continuous passive: is being + developed.

gaps.sentence: By this time tomorrow, the results ___ to every candidate.
gaps.explanation: 'By this time tomorrow' requires future perfect passive: will have been + emailed.

gaps.sentence: A decision ___ once all the evidence has been reviewed.
gaps.explanation: The decision cannot make itself: future passive will be + made.

gaps.sentence: She ___ (think) to be the finest violinist of her generation.
gaps.explanation: Impersonal passive: is thought to be. The thinkers are general, not stated.

gaps.sentence: Several issues remain ___ (resolve) before the launch.
gaps.explanation: 'Remain' + passive infinitive (to be resolved) expresses unfinished business.
